query: What anchor statements will define low/moderate/high RoB for selection, confounding, measurement, and reporting domains to ensure reproducible ratings?

response.query: What anchor statements will define low/moderate/high RoB for selection, confounding, measurement, and reporting domains to ensure reproducible ratings?
response.answer: Low RoB for selection, confounding, measurement, and reporting domains indicates minimal bias, high validity, and transparent reporting. Moderate RoB suggests some bias, but findings are still useful. High RoB implies significant bias, limiting study conclusions.

results.title: PRISMA 2020 explanation and elaboration: updated guidance and exemplars for reporting systematic reviews
results.content: **_Explanation:_** Authors should provide a detailed description of the information sources, such as bibliographic databases, registers and reference lists that were searched or consulted, including the dates when each source was last searched, to allow readers to assess the completeness and currency of the systematic review, and facilitate updating.[40](https://www.bmj.com/content/372/bmj.n160#ref-40) Authors should fully report the “what, when, and how” of the sources searched; the “what” and “when” are covered in item #6, and the “how” is covered in item #7.
